mantra.line: Standards are speed: every ruled format is a decision nobody makes twice. That is the whole edge you named.
One register, tiered the way NASA tiers: policy, procedural requirement, standard, handbook. The house already has all four; it has not called them that.
Derive standards from work already done, the way SOP §8 grows a row per catch. Never write a standard ahead of the work: that is the stall pattern in a suit.

frago.mission: Build and keep a networked library of standards, outside and house-made, at every level from the house down to the project, **in order to** give the operation the speed of never deciding a format twice, and to give the story systems the societies they need.
frago.order: **Read the register, then rule the house ladder.** NASA four is the recommendation (policy → procedural requirement → standard → handbook). The ladder now has a tenant waiting: BOLO 53's development standard sits at rung STANDARD until the tiers are named.
frago.default: Silence: the register sits beside the locus; the development standard keeps its provisional rung; nothing else house-side is filed until the ladder is ruled.

paragraphs.name: Situation
paragraphs.plain: What you found, what you asked, and where it stands.

strand.last: A deep-research session on standards bodies; a harvest of about 65 links.
strand.plan: Bank the harvest, pull what each link holds, organize by domain and tier, map to the house.
strand.you: You said every level is a standards organization and this is a campaign.

items.t: **"What I've been doing right now is just the standards of the organization and the process and application of everything."** The SOP, the project flow, the marking SOP, the WATCH register, the character system, the lattice: all house standards, none filed as such.

**Every level is a standards body:** the house (BLACK · ORANGE · OPERATOR), and inside the projects: DCUS has rules, Trash Land is a DMZ, ASTRO7EX has a cuisine. "The greatest dynamic of story is the battle between the individual and society for freedom and standard."
**The ask:** most links are lists, not standards. Pull whatever each one holds; organize it the best way possible. This is the research phase of a campaign.

**The harvest banked** as a locus on the BOLO 41 convention: _0.1_BVX_LEARN/LOCI/standards.locus.md, every link grouped (single standards · industry lists · organizations and catalogs · the NASA and MIL families).

**The register landed** — `standards.register.md`: how nine bodies tier their documents · one table of about 65 rows by domain, mapped to house areas (lighting and human factors 12 · quality 9 · aerospace and defense 7 · imaging and print 6 · security and privacy 5 · software and systems 5 · metadata 5 · risk and management 4 · AI 3 · symbols 2 · project management 1 · reference-only 6) · the gaps · the free sources. Every ANSI webstore page returned 403; those rows are built from search snippets and slug decoding, flagged in the Source column.

**Three findings that matter:** ESTA's E1.x entertainment-tech standards are free (donation-funded), a clean WARROOM lighting resource · the IES lighting cluster, the harvest's biggest, is paid-only, no free tier · EverySpec plus DLA ASSIST mirror every DoD and NASA directive tier for free, the strongest anchor for the house ladder. NATO NSO's public page 404'd; SAE AS264F's scope is unconfirmed.

**9/15 · BOLO 53 opened and filed.** The house's own development standard (the boresight → how-copy → build → FRAGO loop as an iterative-incremental life cycle) is on disk beside the project flow. Its rung is STANDARD, provisional: the placement is ruled, the ladder it sits on is not.

paragraphs.name: Execution
paragraphs.plain: Research first. Nothing house-side is written until the register is read.

strand.plan: Pull, read, rule the ladder, file what exists, then derive.
strand.you: Phase 3 is a reading and one ruling.

paragraphs.main_effort: The register, read. Everything else waits on it.

phases.t: **The pull** — one agent, 38 calls, the register file.
**Read and rule the house ladder** — NASA four or DoD three.

**File what exists** — SOP · project flow · marking SOP · WATCH register · lattice · character system · the rest. One filed early on Papi's open: the development standard (BOLO 53, 9/15) at rung STANDARD, provisional.
**The story side** — each world's standards body as a canon node (DCUS · Trash Land · ASTRO7EX), the individual-versus-society dynamic written as the setting system's S12 invariant.
**The network** — links between rungs, projects and outside parents; browsable on the WARROOM pattern.

coord: Filed on the LOCI convention (BOLO 41): locus × methods × neighbors × feeds × sources × tier.
Derive from work done; never write a standard ahead of the work.
Free copies first: EverySpec, NASA NODIS, DSP ASSIST, NATO NSO. Paywalled ISO text is never needed for the ladder, only for the content of a specific standard.

strand.last: Two files in the locus folder.
strand.plan: The register grows; the ladder gets its own file when ruled.
strand.you: Zero dollars; ISO text stays unbought.
The ladder, the filing, the name.
